literature.lead_zh: 本期沙粒病毒科研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 中等水平的流动性抑制会促进空间异质性,即使在连接良好的网络中也会导致持久的感染热点。在人与人之间的 传播 不足以持续存在的情况下,环境 传播 进一步维持感染。 [10.1007/s10441-026-09537-4]
提供的证据没有明确说明直接观察到的主要结果。 [10.12688/wellcomeopenres.25937.2]
67%的受访者听说过拉沙热,58.4%的人知道老鼠就是媒介;58.6%的人知道这种疾病是致命的,53.0%的人知道它是可以治疗的,51.9%的人知道它是可以生存的;43%的人说它可以在人与人之间传播,63.7%的人吃老鼠。 [10.53771/ijbpsa.2026.12.1.0067]
累计报告疑似病例1910例,确诊368例。确诊病例病死率为33.97%,逐年上升。近一半(49.7%)来自阿巴卡利基地方政府区(LGA),呈现聚集的空间格局。 [10.1371/journal.pgph.0006871]
调查结果显示,TC 之间在能力、分区和服务整合方面存在重大差异,这对感染控制、员工安全和包容性产生影响。 [10.36253/techne-18620]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Intermediate levels of mobility suppression encourage spatial heterogeneity, resulting in long-lasting infection hotspots even in well-connected networks. Environmental transmission further sustains infection in regimes where human-to-human transmission alone is insufficient for persistence. [10.1007/s10441-026-09537-4]
The supplied evidence does not clearly state a directly observed main result. [10.12688/wellcomeopenres.25937.2]

Sixty-seven percent of the respondents had heard about Lassa fever, and 58.4% knew that rat is the vector; 58.6% knew the disease is deadly, 53.0% knew it is treatable, and 51.9% knew it is survivable; 43% said it can be transmitted from person to person, and 63.7% eat rats. [10.53771/ijbpsa.2026.12.1.0067]

A total of 1,910 suspected cases were reported, with 368 confirmed. The case fatality rate (CFR) among confirmed cases was 33.97%, increasing yearly. Nearly half (49.7%) were from Abakaliki Local Government Area (LGA), showing a clustered spatial pattern. [10.1371/journal.pgph.0006871]

papers.title: Scaling Lassa Virus Dynamics within Anthropogenic Ecosystems (SCAPES) Study Protocol: a mixed-methods observational cohort study of humans, rodents, and landscapes in Nigeria.
papers.abstract: Introduction Zoonotic spillover driven by human activity remains a critical challenge to human health. Research focusing on disease ecology or human–animal interactions provides detailed local insights, but these findings are often siloed and disconnected from global processes and policy. Broad-scale maps of predicted disease risk are more commonly used to inform decisions, yet their connection to local-scale drivers of pathogen transmission remains poorly understood. This study bridges these gaps through a cross-scale study of Lassa fever, a rodent-borne haemorrhagic fever of public health significance in West Africa and a WHO priority pathogen. We use a fine-scale quantitative and participatory modelling approach that explicitly integrates into broad-scale risk models to identify the patterns and processes that drive spillover within human-driven ecosystems. Lassa fever epidemics are dominated by endemic and seasonal transmission of Mammarenavirus lassaense (LASV) from rodent reservoirs to humans within a rural context, positioning LASV as a uniquely tractable system in which to study zoonotic spillover. Methods and Analysis We describe parallel longitudinal observational studies of humans, rodents, and landscapes that are explicitly designed to feed into a cross-scale quantitative modelling framework. By integrating data on landcover, rodent dynamics, human behavior, and LASV infection, we examine how anthropogenic activities shape LASV ecology and human exposure. These data will inform spatial models of the human-rodent-LASV interface to predict key drivers of human exposure risk. Emergent patterns from these models will then be integrated into an existing broad-scale regression-based risk model, extending fine scale mechanism to regional prediction. Together, our empirical research and model predictions will clarify how zoonotic risk propagates from local to regional scales, providing evidence to inform disease management efforts for Lassa fever and zoonotic spillover more broadly.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介 由人类活动驱动的人畜共患病 跨物种溢出 仍然是对人类健康的严峻挑战。专注于疾病生态学或人与动物相互作用的研究提供了详细的本地见解,但这些发现往往是孤立的,并且与全球进程和政策脱节。预测疾病风险的大范围地图更常用于为决策提供信息,但它们与病原体 传播 的局部规模驱动因素的联系仍知之甚少。这项研究通过对 拉沙热 的跨规模研究弥补了这些差距,拉沙热 是一种在西非具有公共卫生意义的啮齿动物传播的出血热,也是世界卫生组织的优先病原体。我们使用精细规模的定量和参与式建模方法,该方法明确地集成到大规模风险模型中,以确定在人类驱动的生态系统中驱动 跨物种溢出 的模式和过程。拉沙热 流行病以哺乳动物拉萨病毒 (LASV) 的地方性和季节性 传播 为主导,从啮齿动物 储存宿主 到农村地区的人类,将 LASV 定位为研究人畜共患 跨物种溢出 的独特易处理系统。方法和分析我们描述了对人类、啮齿动物和景观的平行纵向观察研究,这些研究明确设计用于跨尺度定量建模框架。通过整合土地覆盖、啮齿动物动态、人类行为和 LASV 感染的数据,我们研究了人类活动如何影响 LASV 生态和人类暴露。这些数据将为人类-啮齿动物-LASV 界面的空间模型提供信息,以预测人类暴露风险的关键驱动因素。然后,这些模型中的涌现模式将被集成到现有的基于大规模回归的风险模型中,将精细尺度机制扩展到区域预测。我们的实证研究和模型预测将共同阐明人畜共患风险如何从地方传播到区域尺度,为更广泛地为 拉沙热 和人畜共患 跨物种溢出 的疾病管理工作提供证据。

papers.title: Temporal trends and epidemiological patterns of Lassa fever outbreaks in Ebonyi State, Nigeria: A retrospective study (2018-2023).
papers.abstract: Ebonyi State in southeastern Nigeria has experienced a notably high number of deaths from Lassa fever (LF). Despite this, there is a dearth of studies on the epidemiological and management outcomes of LF outbreaks over the years. The study aims to describe and analyze the epidemiological and management factors of LF for a period of six years (2018-2023) in Ebonyi State with a view to informing targeted interventions, control, and prevention of LF in the state. Secondary data of the LF outbreak from January 2018 to December 2023 were obtained from the Ebonyi State Ministry of Health. The primary outcome was survival from LF, assessed by identifying predictors through logistic regression and estimating survival probability using survival analysis. Associations between demographic and clinical variables were evaluated using odds ratios, chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests. Geospatial mapping with ArcGIS explored the spatial distribution of LF cases. A total of 1,910 suspected cases were reported, with 368 confirmed. The case fatality rate (CFR)among confirmed cases was 33.97%, increasing yearly. Nearly half (49.7%) were from Abakaliki Local Government Area (LGA), showing a clustered spatial pattern. The median age was 32 years (IQR: 22-42), with 52.7% male. Dehydration (OR: 0.45), nausea/vomiting (OR: 0.57), neurologic disorders (OR: 0.33), bleeding (OR: 0.48), sepsis (OR: 0.39), and respiratory disorders (OR: 0.44) significantly reduced survival odds. Median time from symptom onset to hospital presentation was 10 days (IQR: 7-18), and from presentation to diagnosis was 12 days (IQR: 4-23). The CFR of LF in Ebonyi State is high, with Abakaliki LGA as the hotspot. Delays in hospital presentation and diagnosis exist. Regular community sensitization and improved training of medical personnel are needed to promote early symptom reporting and enhance timely LF management.

papers.title: Spatial Pattern Formation in a Reaction Diffusion Model of Lassa Fever with Adaptive Mobility and Environmental Spillover
papers.abstract: Zoonotic diseases, such as Lassa fever, have complicated spatiotemporal dynamics that are influenced by human migration, behavioural responses to infection risk, and environmental transmission via animal reservoirs. Classical spatial epidemic models frequently assume static mobility and ignore the link between disease frequency and movement, limiting their ability to capture geographical variability. In this paper, we present a network-based reaction-diffusion model in which human mobility adjusts to local infection incidence, while infection pressure is maintained via zoonotic spillover and environmental contamination. The model analysis shows that adaptive mobility reorganizes epidemic spread into multiple dynamical regimes, such as homogenized diffusion, wave-like propagation, spatial localization, and suppression-driven extinction. Intermediate levels of mobility suppression encourage spatial heterogeneity, resulting in long-lasting infection hotspots even in well-connected networks. Environmental transmission further sustains infection in regimes where human-to-human transmission alone is insufficient for persistence. To quantify long-term outcomes, we introduce measures of cumulative infection burden, environmental exposure, and spatial dominance across parameter space. The findings underscore the possible limitations of mobility suppression as a management method in endemic zoonotic settings, as well as the importance of environmental transmission in determining disease dynamics. This concept sheds fresh light on spillover-driven persistence and hotspot generation in spatially structured populations.

full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Zoonotic diseases, such as Lassa fever, have complicated spatiotemporal dynamics that are influenced by human migration, behavioural responses to infection risk, and environmental transmission via animal reservoirs. Classical spatial epidemic models frequently assume static mobility and ignore the link between disease frequency and movement, limiting their ability to capture geographical variability. In this paper, we present a network-based reaction-diffusion model in which human mobility adjusts to local infection incidence, while infection pressure is maintained via zoonotic spillover and environmental contamination. The model analysis shows that adaptive mobility reorganizes epidemic spread into multiple dynamical regimes, such as homogenized diffusion, wave-like propagation, spatial localization, and suppression-driven extinction. Intermediate levels of mobility suppression encourage spatial heterogeneity, resulting in long-lasting infection hotspots even in well-connected networks. Environmental transmission further sustains infection in regimes where human-to-human transmission alone is insufficient for persistence. To quantify long-term outcomes, we introduce measures of cumulative infection burden, environmental exposure, and spatial dominance across parameter space. The findings underscore the possible limitations of mobility suppression as a management method in endemic zoonotic settings, as well as the importance of environmental transmission in determining disease dynamics. This concept sheds fresh light on spillover-driven persistence and hotspot generation in spatially structured populations. Data Availability The original contributions presented in this study are included in the article. Further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding author. analysis.research_question_and_background: Zoonotic diseases, such as Lassa fever, have complicated spatiotemporal dynamics influenced by human migration, behavioural responses to infection risk, and environmental transmission via animal reservoirs. Classical spatial epidemic models frequently assume static mobility and ignore the link between disease frequency and movement, limiting their ability to capture geographical variability.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study presents a network-based reaction-diffusion model in which human mobility adjusts to local infection incidence, while infection pressure is maintained via zoonotic spillover and environmental contamination. The model analysis shows that adaptive mobility reorganizes epidemic spread into multiple dynamical regimes, such as homogenized diffusion, wave-like propagation, spatial localization, and suppression-driven extinction.
analysis.methods: To quantify long-term outcomes, the study introduces measures of cumulative infection burden, environmental exposure, and spatial dominance across parameter space. The model incorporates adaptive mobility and environmental transmission to capture the complex dynamics of Lassa fever in spatially structured populations.
analysis.main_results: Intermediate levels of mobility suppression encourage spatial heterogeneity, resulting in long-lasting infection hotspots even in well-connected networks. Environmental transmission further sustains infection in regimes where human-to-human transmission alone is insufficient for persistence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings underscore the possible limitations of mobility suppression as a management method in endemic zoonotic settings, as well as the importance of environmental transmission in determining disease dynamics. This concept sheds fresh light on spillover-driven persistence and hotspot generation in spatially structured populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the need for considering environmental transmission and adaptive mobility in designing control strategies for Lassa fever, as mobility suppression alone may not be effective in eliminating hotspots. These insights can inform surveillance and intervention strategies in endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mathematical model without empirical validation, which limits the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the theoretical nature of the analysis and the lack of real-world data.

analysis.summary_en: This study develops a network-based reaction-diffusion model to explore the spatiotemporal dynamics of Lassa fever, incorporating adaptive human mobility and environmental transmission. The model reveals that intermediate mobility suppression leads to persistent infection hotspots, while environmental transmission sustains infection where human-to-human transmission is insufficient. The findings suggest that mobility suppression alone may be ineffective in endemic settings, emphasizing the need for integrated control strategies that address both human mobility and environmental contamination. The study provides theoretical insights into hotspot generation and persistence in spatially structured populations, with implications for surveillance and intervention design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人畜共患疾病,例如 拉沙热,具有复杂的时空动态,受到人类迁徙、对感染风险的行为反应以及动物 储存宿主 的环境 传播 的影响。经典的空间流行病模型经常假设静态流动性,而忽略疾病频率和流动之间的联系,限制了它们捕捉地理变异性的能力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究提出了一种基于网络的反应扩散模型,其中人类流动性根据局部感染 发病率 进行调整,而感染压力则通过人畜共患 跨物种溢出 和环境污染来维持。模型分析表明,自适应流动将流行病传播重组为多种动态机制,例如均质扩散、波状传播、空间定位和抑制驱动的灭绝。
elements_zh.methods: 为了量化长期结果,该研究引入了累积感染负担、环境暴露和跨参数空间的空间优势的测量方法。该模型结合了自适应移动性和环境 传播,以捕获空间结构人群中 拉沙热 的复杂动态。
elements_zh.main_results: 中等水平的流动性抑制会促进空间异质性,即使在连接良好的网络中也会导致持久的感染热点。在人与人之间的 传播 不足以持续存在的情况下,环境 传播 进一步维持感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了在地方性人畜共患病环境中,移动抑制作为一种管理方法可能存在的局限性,以及环境 传播 在确定疾病动态方面的重要性。这个概念为空间结构群体中 跨物种溢出 驱动的持久性和热点生成提供了新的线索。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调在设计 传播 控制策略时需要考虑环境 传播 和自适应移动性,因为单独移动性抑制可能无法有效消除热点。这些见解可以为 监测 和流行地区的干预策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于未经实证验证的数学模型,这限制了研究结果的普遍性。由于分析的理论性质和缺乏现实世界数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Lassa fever: A review of three treatment centres in Nigeria
papers.abstract: During Lassa fever outbreaks, Treatment Centres (TCs) are critical for patient care and transmission control, yet their design remains underexplored. The study analyses three TC in Nigeria, using a reverse-engineering approach. Findings reveal major differences in capacity, zoning, and service integration, with implications for infection control, staff safety, and inclusivity. Recurring layout trends and critical gaps are identified. A set of spatial indicators is proposed and cross-case results are translated into design principles for LF centres. The work offers a framework for developing design standards to strengthen outbreak management, and highlights the need for adaptable facilities and future research to define indicators linking design with health outcomes and patient experience.
papers.journal: TECHNE - Journal of Technology for Architecture and Environment

papers.title: Knowledge and preventive practices of Lassa fever among residents of Ife-Odan Community, Osun State, South-West Nigeria
papers.abstract: Lassa fever is a disease of public health importance with high mortality and morbidity especially among rural dwellers. Lassa fever is an acute viral hemorrhagic fever caused by Lassa virus. The virus is a single-stranded RNA virus which belongs to the virus family Arenaviridae. It is an old-world arena virus, which is enveloped, single-stranded, and bi-segmented RNA. Lassa fever is a zoonotic disease, the animal reservoir of Lassa virus is a rodent of the genus Mastomys, commonly known as the “multimammate rat.” Mastomys rats infected with Lassa virus do not become ill, but they can shed the virus in their urine and faeces for the rest of their lifetime creating ample opportunity for exposure and transmission The study is a cross-sectional study which was carried out in Ife-Odan community. Ife-Odan, It is a rural community, a town in Osun State which has its headquarters in Ejigbo local government area. The population of Ife-Odan was estimated to be 372,191 according to the national population census of the LGA according to the 2016 national population census. The Sampling technique that was used for this study is Multi-stage sampling technique. The sample size was calculated using the Leslie Kish formula for estimation of single proportions in a population with more than 10,000 inhabitants. The formula used: N= It was observed that Sixty-seven percent of the respondents had heard about Lassa fever, another 58.4% of them knew that rat is the vector. More than half (58.6%), of the respondents knew that the disease is deadly, treatable (53.0%) and survivable (51.9%). Forty-three percent of them say it can be transmitted from one person to another, about half (50.5%) agreed that spreading food by the road side is a risk factor along with poor refuse disposal and dirty environment (50.9%), bush burning (34.9%) and exposing food stuff at home (53.0%). More individuals identified headache (55.3%) as the symptom of Lassa fever. As regards the preventive practices of the respondents, 63.7% eat rats and 36.7% spread food by the road side. Seventy-seven percent of the respondents clear the bush around their homes regularly. Most of the respondents (81.4%) store their food in covered containers and about half them practice bush burning. Two hundred and sixty-eight (62.3%) of the respondents practice unsanitary waste disposal method (open dumping) and large fraction of the population uses rodenticides (76.0%) to kill rats. Significant association was found between respondent’s demographic characteristics, level of education and surprisingly, marital status. Respondents with categorized knowledge scores were assessed. Individuals who were less than 19years of age were realized to have better knowledge about Lassa fever compared to those in other age groups. It was also recorded that Respondents with tertiary level of education have the best knowledge on Lassa fever. Surprisingly, respondents that are single were found to have better knowledge about Lassa fever compared to the married group. These findings are in contrast with studies assessing marital status and its implications on health shown in a previous study.

The population of Ife-Odan was estimated to be 372,191 according to the national population census of the LGA according to the 2016 national population census. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge and preventive practices of Lassa fever among residents of Ife-Odan Community, Osun State, Nigeria. The study found that 67% of respondents had heard about Lassa fever, with 58.4% knowing rats as the vector. While 58.6% knew the disease is deadly, only 53.0% knew it is treatable. Notably, 63.7% reported eating rats, a key risk factor. The study revealed significant associations between knowledge and demographic factors, with younger age, higher education, and single marital status linked to better knowledge. Despite some positive practices like regular bush clearing (77%) and food storage in covered containers (81.4%), unsanitary waste disposal (62.3%) remains a concern. The findings highlight the need for targeted health education to improve preventive practices in rural communities.

papers.title: Impact of Comorbidities on Lassa Fever Outcomes: A 7-Year Retrospective Analysis of Cases Managed at Infection Control and Research Centre FMC Owo
papers.abstract: Background: Lassa fever (LF) remains a major public health challenge in West Africa, particularly Nigeria, where recurrent outbreaks contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality. Although most infections are mild or asymptomatic, severe disease may involve multi-organ dysfunction and poor outcomes. The influence of underlying comorbidities on disease severity remains inadequately characterised, despite its relevance to clinical management and risk stratification. Objective: To determine the prevalence of comorbidities and assess their effect on Lassa fever severity and clinical outcomes among patients managed at a tertiary isolation centre in Nigeria. Methods: This retrospective analytical study reviewed medical records of confirmed Lassa fever cases managed at the Infection Control and Research Centre, Federal Medical Centre, Owo, from 2018 to 2024. A total of 131 patients with documented comorbidities were included. Socio-demographic characteristics, comorbid conditions, and clinical outcomes were extracted using a structured checklist. Data were analysed using SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics summarised patient characteristics, while chi-square and likelihood ratio tests assessed associations. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of disease severity, with statistical significance set at p

analysis.scope_and_question: This study focuses on Lassa fever, a viral hemorrhagic fever caused by Lassa virus, in human patients in Nigeria. The central question is to determine the prevalence of comorbidities and their effect on disease severity and clinical outcomes among patients managed at a tertiary isolation centre.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a retrospective analytical study of confirmed Lassa fever cases managed at the Infection Control and Research Centre, Federal Medical Centre, Owo, Nigeria, from 2018 to 2024. Data from 131 patients with documented comorbidities were extracted using a structured checklist and analysed using SPSS version 27, with descriptive statistics and chi-square, likelihood ratio tests, and multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identifies that comorbidities are prevalent among Lassa fever patients and aims to assess their independent effect on disease severity and clinical outcomes, though specific pooled estimates or stable conclusions are not detailed in the provided evidence.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The influence of underlying comorbidities on Lassa fever severity remains inadequately characterised, representing a concrete evidence gap. The study acknowledges this limitation but does not report specific conflicting findings or heterogeneity in the provided evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings aim to inform clinical management and risk stratification of Lassa fever by elucidating the impact of comorbidities, potentially guiding targeted interventions and improved patient care in endemic regions.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study investigates the impact of comorbidities on Lassa fever outcomes in Nigeria over a 7-year period. Focusing on 131 confirmed cases at a tertiary centre, it examines how underlying health conditions influence disease severity and clinical outcomes. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how comorbidities affect Lassa fever management and risk stratification. By analysing socio-demographic and clinical data through statistical methods, the study aims to provide evidence-based insights for improving patient care and clinical decision-making in Lassa-endemic areas. The findings could help identify high-risk patients and tailor treatment approaches more effectively.

papers.title: ViralMap: predicting features in viral proteins from primary sequence.
papers.abstract: Modern viral vaccines are designed to elicit an immune response against viral proteins that mediate infection, making those proteins important targets for characterization and engineering. To improve vaccine efficacy, the proteins often require changes to specific residues or domains to enhance immunogenicity and induce a protective response. These engineering strategies vary significantly across viruses, making comprehensive and accurate protein sequence annotation a crucial step for guiding vaccine design. The growing risk of novel pathogen emergence and initiatives such as the CEPI 100 Days Mission to rapidly counter "Disease X" threats heighten the need for tools that can convert viral protein sequences from newly characterized genomes or emerging variants into the annotation profiles required for antigen engineering. To address this, we developed ViralMap, a multi-label annotation model tailored for eukaryotic viral proteins. By leveraging ESM-2 language model representations, ViralMap simultaneously predicts 10 distinct annotation classes spanning domain topology and localization, post-translational modifications, and structural features directly from primary sequences. The model achieves a residue-level precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.75 or greater for 7 of the 10 classes, with performance competitive with established tools across the eight benchmarked classes. Case studies on complex glycoproteins from SARS-CoV-2, HIV-1, Nipah virus, and Lassa virus demonstrate the model's ability to predict detailed residue-level annotation profiles, including for proteins from viral families not seen during training. By providing a unified, sequence-based framework for multi-label annotation, ViralMap offers a practical bridge from raw viral protein sequences to the annotation profiles required for antigen engineering.IMPORTANCEThe rapid characterization of viral proteins is critical for developing vaccines against emerging pathogens. When a new strain or virus is identified, researchers need to efficiently identify key features of these proteins to guide vaccine design. Currently, obtaining such features requires running multiple computational tools, which are generally not specialized for viruses that affect humans. ViralMap is a deep learning model that addresses this gap by predicting ten functionally relevant protein annotations simultaneously from sequence alone. Trained specifically on eukaryotic viral proteins, ViralMap aims to support the early stages of vaccine engineering for pandemic preparedness efforts.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了 ViralMap,这是一种专门为真核病毒蛋白定制的多标签注释模型,使用 ESM-2 语言模型表示直接从一级序列预测蛋白质特征。
elements_zh.methods: ViralMap 利用 ESM-2 语言模型表示同时预测 10 个不同的注释类别,包括域拓扑、本地化、翻译后修饰和病毒蛋白序列的结构特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 该模型在 10 个注释类别中的 7 个类别中实现了 0.75 或更高的残基级精确召回曲线下面积 (PR-AUC),其性能可与 8 个基准类别的现有工具相媲美。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 ViralMap 解释为从原始病毒蛋白序列到抗原工程所需注释图谱的实用桥梁,证明其能够预测训练期间未见的病毒家族蛋白的详细残基水平注释。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: ViralMap 通过提供统一的、基于序列的多标签注释框架来支持大流行的防范工作,从而能够有效识别关键蛋白质特征,以指导 疫苗 设计针对新出现的病原体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究证明了与现有工具相比具有较高的证据强度和竞争性能,以及对来自多个病毒家族的复杂糖蛋白的成功案例研究,尽管没有明确报告对非真核病毒的普遍性的局限性。

papers.title_zh: ViralMap:根据一级序列预测病毒蛋白的特征。
papers.source_body_en: Modern viral vaccines are designed to elicit an immune response against viral proteins that mediate infection, making those proteins important targets for characterization and engineering. To improve vaccine efficacy, the proteins often require changes to specific residues or domains to enhance immunogenicity and induce a protective response. These engineering strategies vary significantly across viruses, making comprehensive and accurate protein sequence annotation a crucial step for guiding vaccine design. The growing risk of novel pathogen emergence and initiatives such as the CEPI 100 Days Mission to rapidly counter "Disease X" threats heighten the need for tools that can convert viral protein sequences from newly characterized genomes or emerging variants into the annotation profiles required for antigen engineering. To address this, we developed ViralMap, a multi-label annotation model tailored for eukaryotic viral proteins. By leveraging ESM-2 language model representations, ViralMap simultaneously predicts 10 distinct annotation classes spanning domain topology and localization, post-translational modifications, and structural features directly from primary sequences. The model achieves a residue-level precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.75 or greater for 7 of the 10 classes, with performance competitive with established tools across the eight benchmarked classes. Case studies on complex glycoproteins from SARS-CoV-2, HIV-1, Nipah virus, and Lassa virus demonstrate the model's ability to predict detailed residue-level annotation profiles, including for proteins from viral families not seen during training. By providing a unified, sequence-based framework for multi-label annotation, ViralMap offers a practical bridge from raw viral protein sequences to the annotation profiles required for antigen engineering.IMPORTANCEThe rapid characterization of viral proteins is critical for developing vaccines against emerging pathogens. When a new strain or virus is identified, researchers need to efficiently identify key features of these proteins to guide vaccine design. Currently, obtaining such features requires running multiple computational tools, which are generally not specialized for viruses that affect humans. ViralMap is a deep learning model that addresses this gap by predicting ten functionally relevant protein annotations simultaneously from sequence alone. Trained specifically on eukaryotic viral proteins, ViralMap aims to support the early stages of vaccine engineering for pandemic preparedness efforts.
papers.abstract_zh: 现代病毒 疫苗 旨在引发针对介导感染的病毒蛋白的 免疫应答,使这些蛋白成为表征和工程的重要目标。为了提高 疫苗 功效,蛋白质通常需要改变特定残基或结构域,以增强免疫原性并诱导保护性反应。这些工程策略在不同病毒之间存在显着差异,使得全面而准确的蛋白质序列注释成为指导 疫苗 设计的关键步骤。新型病原体出现的风险不断增加,以及快速应对“疾病 X”威胁的 CEPI 100 天任务等举措,增加了对能够将病毒蛋白序列从新表征的 基因组 或新兴变体转换为抗原工程所需的注释图谱的工具的需求。为了解决这个问题,我们开发了 ViralMap,一种专为真核病毒蛋白定制的多标签注释模型。通过利用 ESM-2 语言模型表示,ViralMap 可同时预测 10 个不同的注释类别,涵盖领域拓扑和本地化、翻译后修饰以及直接来自主序列的结构特征。该模型在 10 个类别中的 7 个类别中实现了 0.75 或更高的残留水平精确召回曲线下面积 (PR-AUC),其性能可与 8 个基准类别中的现有工具相媲美。针对 SARS-CoV-2、HIV-1、尼帕病毒和拉沙病毒的复杂糖蛋白的案例研究表明,该模型能够预测详细的残基水平注释谱,包括来自训练期间未见的病毒家族的蛋白质。通过为多标签注释提供统一的、基于序列的框架,ViralMap 提供了从原始病毒蛋白序列到抗原工程所需的注释图谱的实用桥梁。重要性病毒蛋白的快速表征对于开发针对新兴病原体的 疫苗 至关重要。当识别出新毒株或病毒时,研究人员需要有效识别这些蛋白质的关键特征,以指导 疫苗 设计。目前,获得这些特征需要运行多种计算工具,这些工具通常不是专门针对影响人类的病毒的。ViralMap 是一种深度学习模型,它通过仅根据序列同时预测十个功能相关的蛋白质注释来解决这一差距。ViralMap 专门针对真核病毒蛋白进行了培训,旨在支持 疫苗 工程的早期阶段,以应对大流行病的准备工作。

papers.title: Toward a Pan-Arenavirus T-cell Vaccine: Identification and Preclinical Evaluation of Conserved Epitope constructs 2260477
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Arenaviruses represent a rapidly expanding group of rodent-borne emerging human pathogens with significant pandemic potential. Diseases caused by these viruses, such as the Old-World Arenavirus (OWA) Lassa virus (LASV), which causes Lassa Fever, and the New-World Arenavirus (NWA) Junin virus (JUNV), which causes hemorrhagic fevers, currently lack effective therapeutics or vaccines. Members of the Arenaviridae family possess bi- or tri-segmented genomes encoding three to four viral proteins: glycoprotein (GP), nucleoprotein (NP), RNA polymerase (L) and matrix protein (Z). A robust T-cell immune response is critical for viral clearance and for limiting disease severity during the early stages of the infection. Methods Using a primary in vitro immunogenicity assay, we identified Conserved T cell Epitope Regions (CTERs) derived from conserved sequences within OWA and NWA, using LASV and JUNV as respective prototypes. These CTER epitopes were strongly recognized by human CD4+ T cells in vitro and were predicted to provide broad population coverage across diverse ethnicities. CTER constructs were designed based on the number of viral proteins included (GP+N+L, N+L, or L) and were assembled using AlphaFold into stable and unstable forms. Plasmids for OWA and NWA were codon-optimized and subsequently packaged into mRNA constructs. Results Our ongoing BDF1 mouse studies demonstrate that the CTER-based T-cell vaccine is both safe and immunogenic, as assessed using a combined activation-induced marker (AIM) and intracellular cytokine (ICS) assay. AIM+ T cells isolated from the spleen and lymph nodes show strong cross-reactive potential across the Arenaviridae family. Conclusion With further in vitro and in vivo evaluation, this work represents an initial step toward the development of a pan-arenavirus T-cell vaccine. Funding Source CEPI, NIH Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arenaviruses represent a rapidly expanding group of rodent-borne emerging human pathogens with significant pandemic potential, and diseases caused by these viruses, such as Lassa Fever and hemorrhagic fevers, currently lack effective therapeutics or vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used BDF1 mouse models to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a CTER-based T-cell vaccine, with constructs designed based on viral proteins (GP+N+L, N+L, or L) and assembled into stable and unstable forms using AlphaFold.
analysis.methods: Using a primary in vitro immunogenicity assay, conserved T cell epitope regions (CTERs) were identified from Old-World and New-World Arenaviruses, and plasmids were codon-optimized and packaged into mRNA constructs for evaluation.
analysis.main_results: The CTER-based T-cell vaccine demonstrated safety and immunogenicity in BDF1 mouse studies, with AIM+ T cells showing strong cross-reactive potential across the Arenaviridae family.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this work as an initial step toward the development of a pan-arenavirus T-cell vaccine, with CTER epitopes strongly recognized by human CD4+ T cells and predicted to provide broad population coverage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This research informs the development of a broadly protective T-cell vaccine against arenaviruses, which could address the lack of effective therapeutics or vaccines for diseases like Lassa Fever and hemorrhagic fevers.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the urgent need for effective vaccines against arenaviruses, which are emerging human pathogens with pandemic potential. Researchers identified conserved T cell epitope regions (CTERs) from Old-World and New-World Arenaviruses and developed mRNA-based vaccine constructs. Preclinical evaluation in BDF1 mice demonstrated that the vaccine is safe and immunogenic, with T cells showing cross-reactive potential across the Arenaviridae family. The CTER epitopes were strongly recognized by human CD4+ T cells and predicted to provide broad population coverage. While this represents a promising initial step toward a pan-arenavirus T-cell vaccine, further evaluation is needed to confirm efficacy in humans.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 沙粒病毒 代表了一组迅速扩大的啮齿动物传播的新兴人类病原体,具有显着的大流行潜力,由这些病毒引起的疾病,如 拉沙热 和出血热,目前缺乏有效的治疗方法或 疫苗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 BDF1 小鼠模型来评估基于 CTER 的 T 细胞 疫苗 的安全性和免疫原性,其构建体基于病毒蛋白(GP+N+L、N+L 或 L)设计,并使用 AlphaFold 组装成稳定和不稳定的形式。
elements_zh.methods: 使用初级体外免疫原性测定,从旧世界和新世界 沙粒病毒 中鉴定出保守的 T 细胞表位区域 (CTER),并对质粒进行密码子优化并包装到 mRNA 构建体中进行评估。

papers.title_zh: 迈向泛 沙粒病毒 T 细胞 疫苗:保守表位构建体的鉴定和临床前评估 2260477
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Arenaviruses represent a rapidly expanding group of rodent-borne emerging human pathogens with significant pandemic potential. Diseases caused by these viruses, such as the Old-World Arenavirus (OWA) Lassa virus (LASV), which causes Lassa Fever, and the New-World Arenavirus (NWA) Junin virus (JUNV), which causes hemorrhagic fevers, currently lack effective therapeutics or vaccines. Members of the Arenaviridae family possess bi- or tri-segmented genomes encoding three to four viral proteins: glycoprotein (GP), nucleoprotein (NP), RNA polymerase (L) and matrix protein (Z). A robust T-cell immune response is critical for viral clearance and for limiting disease severity during the early stages of the infection. Methods Using a primary in vitro immunogenicity assay, we identified Conserved T cell Epitope Regions (CTERs) derived from conserved sequences within OWA and NWA, using LASV and JUNV as respective prototypes. These CTER epitopes were strongly recognized by human CD4+ T cells in vitro and were predicted to provide broad population coverage across diverse ethnicities. CTER constructs were designed based on the number of viral proteins included (GP+N+L, N+L, or L) and were assembled using AlphaFold into stable and unstable forms. Plasmids for OWA and NWA were codon-optimized and subsequently packaged into mRNA constructs. Results Our ongoing BDF1 mouse studies demonstrate that the CTER-based T-cell vaccine is both safe and immunogenic, as assessed using a combined activation-induced marker (AIM) and intracellular cytokine (ICS) assay. AIM+ T cells isolated from the spleen and lymph nodes show strong cross-reactive potential across the Arenaviridae family. Conclusion With further in vitro and in vivo evaluation, this work represents an initial step toward the development of a pan-arenavirus T-cell vaccine. Funding Source CEPI, NIH Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 沙粒病毒 代表了一组迅速扩大的啮齿类动物传播的新出现的人类病原体,具有显着的大流行潜力。由这些病毒引起的疾病,例如引起拉沙热的旧世界沙粒病毒 (OWA)拉沙病毒(LASV)和引起出血热的新世界沙粒病毒 (NWA)胡宁病毒(JUNV),目前缺乏有效的治疗方法或疫苗。沙粒病毒科家族的成员拥有双段或三段基因组,编码三至四种病毒蛋白:糖蛋白(GP)、核蛋白(NP)、RNA聚合酶(L)和基质蛋白(Z)。强大的 T 细胞 免疫应答 对于病毒清除和感染早期限制疾病严重程度至关重要。方法 使用初级体外免疫原性测定,我们使用 LASV 和 JUNV 作为各自的原型,鉴定了源自 OWA 和 NWA 内保守序列的保守 T 细胞表位区域 (CTER)。这些 CTER 表位在体外被人类 CD4+ T 细胞强烈识别,预计将提供跨不同种族的广泛人群覆盖。CTER 构建体是根据包含的病毒蛋白数量(GP+N+L、N+L 或 L)设计的,并使用 AlphaFold 组装成稳定和不稳定的形式。OWA 和 NWA 的质粒经过密码子优化,随后包装成 mRNA 构建体。结果我们正在进行的 BDF1 小鼠研究表明,基于 CTER 的 T 细胞 疫苗 既安全又具有免疫原性,使用组合激活诱导标记物 (AIM) 和细胞内细胞因子 (ICS) 测定进行评估。从脾脏和淋巴结中分离出的 AIM+ T 细胞在 沙粒病毒科 家族中表现出强大的交叉反应潜力。结论 通过进一步的体外和体内评估,这项工作代表了开发泛 沙粒病毒 T 细胞 疫苗 的第一步。资金来源 CEPI、NIH 主题类别 疫苗 和免疫疗法 (VAC)

papers.title: RORα governs CD8+ T cell memory subset specification and offers a therapeutic node for antiviral immunity 2259080
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction The establishment of immunological memory is crucial for durable antiviral immunity and underlies effective vaccine design in enhancing memory responses. The retinoic acid receptor—related orphan receptor α(RORα), a ligand-regulated transcription factor of the nuclear receptor superfamily, has been implicated in CD8+ T cell immunity, yet its role remains poorly defined. Methods To investigate this, we integrated genomic approaches with both genetic and pharmacologic perturbations of RORα to examine its role in CD8+ T cell development during antiviral responses. Results RORα-deficient mice infected with acute lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) exhibited fewer virus-specific CD8+ T cells and higher splenic viral titers at day 5 post-infection than wild-type controls. Despite reduced numbers, RORα-deficient CD8+ T cells showed enhanced cytotoxic potential, indicating that RORα modulates effector programming rather than overall functional capacity. RORα deficiency also led to increased migration and redistribution of CD8+ T cells into non-lymphoid compartments, particularly the liver and adipose tissues, and promoted the development of memory precursors (MP), peripheral memory (TPM), and tissue-resident memory (TRM) populations. Single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq revealed enrichment of transcriptional and chromatin programs linked to MP and TRM gene signatures, including elevated expression of Tcf7 and Runx family members, alongside reduced accessibility at loci governing terminal effector differentiation. Pharmacologic inhibition of RORα with the RORα-selective inverse agonist, SR3335, recapitulated the knockout phenotype, favoring memory CD8+ T cell differentiation over terminal effectors. Conclusion Collectively, our data reveal distinct programming of CD8 T effector versus memory populations attributable to RORα activity. As a ligand-regulated transcription factor, RORα may be a promising target to enhance CD8+ T cell memory responses for improved vaccines and cell-based immunotherapies. Funding Source N/A Topic Categories Immune Response Regulation: Molecular Mechanisms (IRM)

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 免疫记忆的建立对于持久的 抗病毒药物 免疫至关重要,也是增强记忆反应的有效 疫苗 设计的基础。视黄酸受体相关孤儿受体 α (RORα) 是核受体超家族的配体调节转录因子,与 CD8+ T 细胞免疫有关,但其作用仍不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为了研究这一点,该研究将基因组方法与 RORα 的遗传和药理学扰动相结合,以检查其在感染急性 淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 的小鼠 抗病毒药物 反应期间 CD8+ T 细胞发育中的作用。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用基因组方法、遗传扰动和 RORα 选择性反向激动剂 SR3335 对 RORα 的药理学抑制,以检查其在感染 LCMV 的小鼠 抗病毒药物 反应期间 CD8+ T 细胞发育中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 感染 LCMV 的 RORα 缺陷小鼠在感染后第 5 天表现出比野生型对照更少的病毒特异性 CD8+ T 细胞和更高的脾脏病毒滴度。尽管数量减少,但 RORα 缺陷的 CD8+ T 细胞表现出增强的细胞毒性潜力,并且 RORα 缺陷导致 CD8+ T 细胞迁移和重新分布到非淋巴区(特别是肝脏和脂肪组织)的增加,促进记忆前体 (MP)、外周记忆 (TPM) 和组织驻留记忆 (TRM) 群体的发育。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,RORα 活性明显地编程 CD8 T 效应器与记忆群体,这一点可以从 RORα 缺陷细胞中与 MP 和 TRM 基因特征相关的转录和染色质程序的富集来证明,包括 Tcf7 和 Runx 家族成员的表达升高,以及控制终末效应器分化的位点的可及性降低。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 作为配体调节的转录因子,RORα 可能是增强 CD8+ T 细胞记忆反应的有希望的靶标,以改善 疫苗 和基于细胞的免疫疗法,为 抗病毒药物 免疫提供治疗节点。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在小鼠身上进行的,虽然该模型的研究结果是可靠的,但与人类的转化相关性需要进一步研究。由于多种基因组方法以及遗传和药理学扰动的整合,证据强度很高。

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction The establishment of immunological memory is crucial for durable antiviral immunity and underlies effective vaccine design in enhancing memory responses. The retinoic acid receptor—related orphan receptor α(RORα), a ligand-regulated transcription factor of the nuclear receptor superfamily, has been implicated in CD8+ T cell immunity, yet its role remains poorly defined. Methods To investigate this, we integrated genomic approaches with both genetic and pharmacologic perturbations of RORα to examine its role in CD8+ T cell development during antiviral responses. Results RORα-deficient mice infected with acute lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) exhibited fewer virus-specific CD8+ T cells and higher splenic viral titers at day 5 post-infection than wild-type controls. RORα deficiency also led to increased migration and redistribution of CD8+ T cells into non-lymphoid compartments, particularly the liver and adipose tissues, and promoted the development of memory precursors (MP), peripheral memory (TPM), and tissue-resident memory (TRM) populations. Single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq revealed enrichment of transcriptional and chromatin programs linked to MP and TRM gene signatures, including elevated expression of Tcf7 and Runx family members, alongside reduced accessibility at loci governing terminal effector differentiation. Pharmacologic inhibition of RORα with the RORα-selective inverse agonist, SR3335, recapitulated the knockout phenotype, favoring memory CD8+ T cell differentiation over terminal effectors. Conclusion Collectively, our data reveal distinct programming of CD8 T effector versus memory populations attributable to RORα activity. As a ligand-regulated transcription factor, RORα may be a promising target to enhance CD8+ T cell memory responses for improved vaccines and cell-based immunotherapies. papers.title: Broad-spectrum molecular detection of zoonotic agents in wild micromammals: a nationwide surveillance study in the Republic of Korea
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Wild micromammals serve as key hosts for diverse zoonotic pathogens, maintaining these agents in natural ecosystems and facilitating potential spillover to humans. Assessing pathogen prevalence in micromammals is essential for evaluating zoonotic risk and informing public health interventions. Methods In this study, we applied the TaqMan Array Card (TAC) platform, a high-throughput molecular diagnostic tool, to micromammal-borne zoonotic pathogen surveillance. From October to November 2022, a total of 160 wild micromammals, including Apodemus agrarius (Striped field mouse) (90.6, n = 145) and Crocidura lasiura (Ussuri white-toothed shrew) (9.4%, n = 15), were collected from 12 regions. Spleen tissues were screened for 45 viral, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens using the TAC platform. Results Viral pathogens were detected at lower frequencies, including Junin virus (2.5%, n = 4) and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (0.6%, n = 1). In contrast, bacterial pathogens showed high prevalence, including Bartonella spp. (78.8%, n = 126), Ehrlichia spp. (47.5%, n = 76), Anaplasma spp. (46.9%, n = 75), Borrelia spp. (36.3%, n = 58), Orientia tsutsugamushi (25.6%, n = 41), Rickettsia spp. (4.4%, n = 7), and Leptospira spp. (2.5%, n = 4) as well as protozoan pathogens such as Trypanosoma spp. (87.5%, n = 140), Cryptosporidium (20.0%, n = 32), and Toxoplasma gondii (1.3%, n = 2). However, some detections particularly viral pathogens were based solely on the TAC platform and were not confirmed by conventional PCR and sequencing. Phylogenetic analyses of TAC-positive samples revealed the presence of diverse zoonotic agents, including Anaplasma phagocytophilum , Ehrlichia muris , Candidatus Ehrlichia khabarensis, Candidatus Neoehrlichia mikurensis, Borreliella afzelii , Borrelia miyamotoi , O. tsutsugamushi Saitama and Young-worl strains, Bartonella quintana , B. fuyuanensis , and B. Conclusions These findings demonstrate the widespread regional distribution of micromammal-borne zoonotic pathogens across the ROK and provide essential baseline data to support integrated One Health surveillance frameworks for emerging and re-emerging micromammal-borne zoonoses.

From October to November 2022, 160 micromammals were collected from 12 regions, with spleen tissues screened for 45 pathogens. Viral pathogens were detected at low frequencies, including Junin virus (2.5%) and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (0.6%), while bacterial and protozoan pathogens showed high prevalence, such as Bartonella spp. (78.8%), Trypanosoma spp. (87.5%), and Ehrlichia spp. (47.5%). The findings highlight the widespread distribution of micromammal-borne pathogens, providing baseline data for One Health surveillance frameworks. However, some viral detections lacked confirmation by conventional methods, representing a limitation in the study.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Wild micromammals serve as key hosts for diverse zoonotic pathogens, maintaining these agents in natural ecosystems and facilitating potential spillover to humans. Assessing pathogen prevalence in micromammals is essential for evaluating zoonotic risk and informing public health interventions. Methods In this study, we applied the TaqMan Array Card (TAC) platform, a high-throughput molecular diagnostic tool, to micromammal-borne zoonotic pathogen surveillance. From October to November 2022, a total of 160 wild micromammals, including Apodemus agrarius (Striped field mouse) (90.6, n = 145) and Crocidura lasiura (Ussuri white-toothed shrew) (9.4%, n = 15), were collected from 12 regions. Spleen tissues were screened for 45 viral, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens using the TAC platform. Results Viral pathogens were detected at lower frequencies, including Junin virus (2.5%, n = 4) and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (0.6%, n = 1). In contrast, bacterial pathogens showed high prevalence, including Bartonella spp. (78.8%, n = 126), Ehrlichia spp. (47.5%, n = 76), Anaplasma spp. (46.9%, n = 75), Borrelia spp. (36.3%, n = 58), Orientia tsutsugamushi (25.6%, n = 41), Rickettsia spp. (4.4%, n = 7), and Leptospira spp. (2.5%, n = 4) as well as protozoan pathogens such as Trypanosoma spp. (87.5%, n = 140), Cryptosporidium (20.0%, n = 32), and Toxoplasma gondii (1.3%, n = 2). However, some detections particularly viral pathogens were based solely on the TAC platform and were not confirmed by conventional PCR and sequencing. Phylogenetic analyses of TAC-positive samples revealed the presence of diverse zoonotic agents, including Anaplasma phagocytophilum , Ehrlichia muris , Candidatus Ehrlichia khabarensis, Candidatus Neoehrlichia mikurensis, Borreliella afzelii , Borrelia miyamotoi , O. tsutsugamushi Saitama and Young-worl strains, Bartonella quintana , B. fuyuanensis , and B. Conclusions These findings demonstrate the widespread regional distribution of micromammal-borne zoonotic pathogens across the ROK and provide essential baseline data to support integrated One Health surveillance frameworks for emerging and re-emerging micromammal-borne zoonoses.

papers.title: LRRK2 G2019S reprograms innate and adaptive immunity to drive context-dependent host defense outcomes
papers.abstract: Introduction Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a neurological disorder characterized not only by neurodegeneration but also by chronic immune dysregulation across the lifespan. Although the initiating events underlying PD remain unclear, accumulating evidence suggests that inflammatory processes may contribute to disease susceptibility and progression. Mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 ( LRRK2 ), particularly the gain-of-function G2019S variant, represent the common genetic cause of familial PD and have been implicated in immune regulation and infection susceptibility. To date, most research has focused on the effect of LRRK2 mutation in neurons and the contributions of G2019S-mediated kinase activity to neuronal toxicity, leaving the role of G2019S-mediated kinase activity in immune cell homeostasis and its contribution to PD pathogenesis largely unresolved. Methods Here, we used murine overexpression models of wildtype and G2019S variant of mouse Lrrk2 to examine how Lrrk2 G2019S shapes host defense across viral and bacterial infection models. We tested systemic sepsis and Escherichia coli infection to examine bacterial clearance. We followed up by testing macrophage responses to intracellular (Listeria monocytogenes) or primarily extracellular (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) bacteria. Finally, tested antibody-mediated immunity using influenza and cytotoxic T cell-mediated immunity using lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection. Results We found that Lrrk2 G2019S overexpression enhanced survival and bacterial clearance during P. aeruginosa lung infection, whereas the same genotype worsened outcomes in polymicrobial sepsis, with increased mortality, pulmonary myeloid infiltration and a hematopoietic cell-intrinsic phenotype. monocytogenes infection, Lrrk2 G2019S selectively reduced non-classical monocytes without altering disease progression. In influenza and LCMV infection, G2019S altered antigen-specific CD8 + T cell distribution without major changes in cell memory responses clinical severity. Discussion Together, these data show that Lrrk2 G2019S selectively reprograms innate and adaptive immunity in a pathogen- and tissue-dependent manner, uncoupling inflammatory magnitude from effective host defense. These results and previous work support a model in which the G2019S LRRK2 variant contributes to maladaptive inflammatory responses to specific infection challenges, providing insight into how lifetime immune perturbations may intersect with genetic susceptibility to influence lifetime infection risk.

papers.title_zh: LRRK2 G2019S 重新编程先天性和适应性免疫以驱动上下文相关的 宿主 防御结果
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a neurological disorder characterized not only by neurodegeneration but also by chronic immune dysregulation across the lifespan. Although the initiating events underlying PD remain unclear, accumulating evidence suggests that inflammatory processes may contribute to disease susceptibility and progression. Mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 ( LRRK2 ), particularly the gain-of-function G2019S variant, represent the common genetic cause of familial PD and have been implicated in immune regulation and infection susceptibility. To date, most research has focused on the effect of LRRK2 mutation in neurons and the contributions of G2019S-mediated kinase activity to neuronal toxicity, leaving the role of G2019S-mediated kinase activity in immune cell homeostasis and its contribution to PD pathogenesis largely unresolved. Methods Here, we used murine overexpression models of wildtype and G2019S variant of mouse Lrrk2 to examine how Lrrk2 G2019S shapes host defense across viral and bacterial infection models. We tested systemic sepsis and Escherichia coli infection to examine bacterial clearance. We followed up by testing macrophage responses to intracellular (Listeria monocytogenes) or primarily extracellular (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) bacteria. Finally, tested antibody-mediated immunity using influenza and cytotoxic T cell-mediated immunity using lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection. Results We found that Lrrk2 G2019S overexpression enhanced survival and bacterial clearance during P. aeruginosa lung infection, whereas the same genotype worsened outcomes in polymicrobial sepsis, with increased mortality, pulmonary myeloid infiltration and a hematopoietic cell-intrinsic phenotype. monocytogenes infection, Lrrk2 G2019S selectively reduced non-classical monocytes without altering disease progression. In influenza and LCMV infection, G2019S altered antigen-specific CD8 + T cell distribution without major changes in cell memory responses clinical severity. Discussion Together, these data show that Lrrk2 G2019S selectively reprograms innate and adaptive immunity in a pathogen- and tissue-dependent manner, uncoupling inflammatory magnitude from effective host defense. These results and previous work support a model in which the G2019S LRRK2 variant contributes to maladaptive inflammatory responses to specific infection challenges, providing insight into how lifetime immune perturbations may intersect with genetic susceptibility to influence lifetime infection risk.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介 帕金森病 (PD) 越来越被认为是一种神经系统疾病,其特征不仅是神经退行性变,而且还表现为整个生命周期的慢性免疫失调。尽管帕金森病的起始事件尚不清楚,但越来越多的证据表明炎症过程可能会导致疾病的易感性和进展。富含亮氨酸重复激酶 2 ( LRRK2 ) 中的 突变,特别是功能获得性 G2019S 变体,代表了家族性 PD 的常见遗传原因,并且与免疫调节和感染易感性有关。迄今为止,大多数研究都集中在 LRRK2 突变 对神经元的影响以及 G2019S 介导的激酶活性对神经元毒性的贡献上,而 G2019S 介导的激酶活性在免疫细胞稳态中的作用及其对 PD 发病机制 的贡献在很大程度上尚未解决。方法在这里,我们使用小鼠 Lrrk2 野生型和 G2019S 变体的小鼠过表达模型来检查 Lrrk2 G2019S 如何在病毒和细菌感染模型中塑造 宿主 防御。我们测试了系统性脓毒症和大肠杆菌感染,以检查细菌清除情况。我们随后测试了巨噬细胞对细胞内(单核细胞增生李斯特菌)或主要细胞外(铜绿假单胞菌)细菌的反应。最后,使用流感测试了抗体介导的免疫,并使用 淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 感染测试了细胞毒性 T 细胞介导的免疫。结果我们发现,Lrrk2 G2019S 过表达可增强铜绿假单胞菌肺部感染期间的存活率和细菌清除率,而相同的基因型会恶化多种微生物败血症的结果,导致 死亡率 增加、肺骨髓浸润和造血细胞固有表型增加。单核细胞增生李斯特菌感染时,Lrrk2 G2019S 选择性减少非经典单核细胞,而不改变疾病进展。在流感和 LCMV 感染中,G2019S 改变了抗原特异性 CD8 + T 细胞分布,但细胞记忆反应和临床严重程度没有发生重大变化。总之,这些数据表明 Lrrk2 G2019S 以病原体和组织依赖性方式选择性地重新编程先天性和适应性免疫,将炎症程度与有效的 宿主 防御分开。这些结果和之前的工作支持了一个模型,其中 G2019S LRRK2 变体会导致对特定感染挑战的适应不良炎症反应,从而深入了解终生免疫扰动如何与遗传易感性相交叉,从而影响终生感染风险。

papers.title: Impact of Thymus Removal in Altering CD8 T Cell Properties 2260157
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction The thymus supplies naïve T cells to sustain T cell populations, but it gradually shrinks with age, leading to a decline in thymic output. Consequently, cessation of thymic output reduces naïve T cell numbers, raising the question of whether the remaining cells adapt to maintain immune competence. Methods Here, we examined the quantity and quality of antigen-specific CD8 T cells in mice after thymectomy. Results Our experiments showed that thymectomy reduced the number of antigen-specific CD8 T cells. Interestingly, following acute lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, antigen-specific CD8 T cells derived from thymectomized mice exhibited greater expansion and generated more memory cells than those from controls. To explore why CD8 T cells from thymectomized mice possess such augmented expansion capacity, we analyzed these CD8 T cells prior to infection and found significant phenotypic remodeling after thymectomy, thereby altering their subset composition. Virtual memory (VM) cells, which exhibits memory phenotypes yet remain antigen inexperienced, increased within the antigen-specific CD8 T cell pool after thymectomy. In addition, thymectomy altered the phenotypes of antigen-specific naïve CD8 T cells, greatly enriching the IL-18Rα+ CD73+ CXCR3+ subset. Importantly, this subset contributed to the enhanced expansion of antigen-specific CD8 T cells after LCMV infection. Conclusion Together, our findings suggest that upon loss of thymic output during thymic involution or thymectomy, antigen-inexperienced CD8 T cells undergo qualitative remodeling, compensating for reduced cell numbers by increasing functionally potent subsets that help preserve antiviral immunity. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

Conclusion Together, our findings suggest that upon loss of thymic output during thymic involution or thymectomy, antigen-inexperienced CD8 T cells undergo qualitative remodeling, compensating for reduced cell numbers by increasing functionally potent subsets that help preserve antiviral immunity. papers.title_zh: 胸腺去除对改变 CD8 T 细胞特性的影响 2260157
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction The thymus supplies naïve T cells to sustain T cell populations, but it gradually shrinks with age, leading to a decline in thymic output. Consequently, cessation of thymic output reduces naïve T cell numbers, raising the question of whether the remaining cells adapt to maintain immune competence. Methods Here, we examined the quantity and quality of antigen-specific CD8 T cells in mice after thymectomy. Results Our experiments showed that thymectomy reduced the number of antigen-specific CD8 T cells. Interestingly, following acute lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, antigen-specific CD8 T cells derived from thymectomized mice exhibited greater expansion and generated more memory cells than those from controls. To explore why CD8 T cells from thymectomized mice possess such augmented expansion capacity, we analyzed these CD8 T cells prior to infection and found significant phenotypic remodeling after thymectomy, thereby altering their subset composition. Virtual memory (VM) cells, which exhibits memory phenotypes yet remain antigen inexperienced, increased within the antigen-specific CD8 T cell pool after thymectomy. In addition, thymectomy altered the phenotypes of antigen-specific naïve CD8 T cells, greatly enriching the IL-18Rα+ CD73+ CXCR3+ subset. Importantly, this subset contributed to the enhanced expansion of antigen-specific CD8 T cells after LCMV infection. Conclusion Together, our findings suggest that upon loss of thymic output during thymic involution or thymectomy, antigen-inexperienced CD8 T cells undergo qualitative remodeling, compensating for reduced cell numbers by increasing functionally potent subsets that help preserve antiviral immunity. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

papers.title: Immune checkpoint blockade enhances CD4 effector function to control persistent viral infection 2267612
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction T cell exhaustion, a defining hallmark of chronic viral infections and cancer, is characterized by the progressive loss of effector function and sustained expression of inhibitory receptors on T cells. Although immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies, such as PD-1 inhibition, can transiently reinvigorate subsets of exhausted CD8+ T cells, their efficacy remains constrained by the limited pool of self-renewing, progenitor-like TCF1+ CXCR5+ CD8+ T cells. We have previously demonstrated that B cell—derived IL-27 signaling is necessary for the expansion and maintenance of this progenitor-like population during chronic infection. Using an IL-27 receptor deficient mouse model, we reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which PD-1 blockade mediates viral clearance. We demonstrate that PD-1 inhibition enhances CD4+ T cell function, specifically through increased IL-21 production from T follicular helper (Tfh) cells which promotes both humoral and cytotoxic antiviral responses. Our findings identify a novel IL-27 independent CD4+ T cell axis through which checkpoint blockade controls persistent viremia. Methods To determine the impact of checkpoint inhibition on persistent viral infection, IL-27 receptor—deficient mice were infected with chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV clone 13) and treated with PD-1 blocking antibodies. We used flow cytometry and viral titers to evaluate CD4+ and CD8+ T cell subsets, the importance of IL-21, and persistent viral clearance. Results PD-1 blockade restored antiviral immunity in IL-27 receptor—deficient mice and resulted in enhanced CD4+ T cell function. We saw increased IL-21 production from T follicular helper cells that led to higher cytotoxic and humoral antiviral responses. Conclusion Our studies reveal that PD-1 blockade can drive persistent viral clearance through an IL-27—independent mechanism that involves IL-21—producing CD4+ T cells. Funding Source N/A Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

papers.title_zh: 免疫检查点阻断增强 CD4 效应器功能以控制持续性病毒感染 2267612
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction T cell exhaustion, a defining hallmark of chronic viral infections and cancer, is characterized by the progressive loss of effector function and sustained expression of inhibitory receptors on T cells. Although immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies, such as PD-1 inhibition, can transiently reinvigorate subsets of exhausted CD8+ T cells, their efficacy remains constrained by the limited pool of self-renewing, progenitor-like TCF1+ CXCR5+ CD8+ T cells. We have previously demonstrated that B cell—derived IL-27 signaling is necessary for the expansion and maintenance of this progenitor-like population during chronic infection. Using an IL-27 receptor deficient mouse model, we reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which PD-1 blockade mediates viral clearance. We demonstrate that PD-1 inhibition enhances CD4+ T cell function, specifically through increased IL-21 production from T follicular helper (Tfh) cells which promotes both humoral and cytotoxic antiviral responses. Our findings identify a novel IL-27 independent CD4+ T cell axis through which checkpoint blockade controls persistent viremia. Methods To determine the impact of checkpoint inhibition on persistent viral infection, IL-27 receptor—deficient mice were infected with chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV clone 13) and treated with PD-1 blocking antibodies. We used flow cytometry and viral titers to evaluate CD4+ and CD8+ T cell subsets, the importance of IL-21, and persistent viral clearance. Results PD-1 blockade restored antiviral immunity in IL-27 receptor—deficient mice and resulted in enhanced CD4+ T cell function. We saw increased IL-21 production from T follicular helper cells that led to higher cytotoxic and humoral antiviral responses. Conclusion Our studies reveal that PD-1 blockade can drive persistent viral clearance through an IL-27—independent mechanism that involves IL-21—producing CD4+ T cells. Funding Source N/A Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

papers.title: Delineating the role of CXCR6 for the formation and maintenance of CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells in the gut 2260742
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction The CXCR6-CXCL16 axis has emerged as a critical regulator of T cell migration across various barrier tissues, thereby shaping localized immune memory. CXCR6 may help maintain the retention and function of CD8+ T cells in multiple tissues after infection, influencing not only immediate effector responses but also the long-term memory landscape of T cell populations. However, definitive in vivo data on the effect of CXCR6 on CD8+ T intraepithelial lymphocytes in the intestine (siIELs) are lacking. Methods Using the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) Armstrong mouse model, we aim to examine the differential effects of CXCR6 deletion in the gut and identify the tissue-specific producers of the CXCR6 ligand, CXCL16. For this, we employ spectral flow cytometry and plan to use bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry imaging, and spatial transcriptomics. Results Preliminary adoptive transfer experiments showed that, when assessed in bulk, the ratio of CXCR6-deficient to wild-type P14 CD8+ T cells was lower among siIELs at day 7 after acute infection. Notably, within this population at the same time point, CXCR6 deficiency led to reduced CD69 expression and a reciprocal increase in CD103. Additionally, CD103+CD69+ KO CD8+ T cells were increased in the gut compared to adoptively transferred WT cells. Meanwhile, the expression of CD127 and KLRG1 remained unchanged. Conclusion Together, these findings suggest that CXCR6 plays a role in maintaining immune homeostasis and supporting the adaptive immune response in the gut during the early stages of acute infection. Funding Source In-institute funding. Topic Categories Lymphocyte Differentiation and Peripheral Maintenance (LYM)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of CXCR6 in the formation and maintenance of CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells in the gut, addressing a knowledge gap regarding its effect on CD8+ T intraepithelial lymphocytes in the intestine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) Armstrong mouse model, the study examined the differential effects of CXCR6 deletion in the gut and identified tissue-specific producers of the CXCR6 ligand, CXCL16.
analysis.methods: The study employed spectral flow cytometry and planned to use bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry imaging, and spatial transcriptomics to analyze the effects of CXCR6 deficiency.
analysis.main_results: Preliminary adoptive transfer experiments showed a lower ratio of CXCR6-deficient to wild-type P14 CD8+ T cells among small intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes at day 7 after acute infection, with reduced CD69 expression and increased CD103 in CXCR6-deficient cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting that CXCR6 plays a role in maintaining immune homeostasis and supporting the adaptive immune response in the gut during the early stages of acute infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the mechanisms of T cell retention in barrier tissues, which could inform strategies for enhancing immune memory in mucosal sites and improving vaccine efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the preliminary nature of the results and the reliance on a single mouse model, with limitations including the lack of definitive in vivo data on CXCR6 effects in the gut.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of CXCR6 in CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells in the gut using the LCMV Armstrong mouse model. Preliminary adoptive transfer experiments revealed that CXCR6 deficiency led to a lower ratio of CXCR6-deficient to wild-type P14 CD8+ T cells among small intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes at day 7 post-infection, with reduced CD69 expression and increased CD103. The authors suggest CXCR6 maintains immune homeostasis and supports adaptive immune responses in the gut during early acute infection. The findings provide insights into T cell retention mechanisms in barrier tissues, potentially informing vaccine strategies, though the evidence is preliminary and based on a single model.

For this, we employ spectral flow cytometry and plan to use bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry imaging, and spatial transcriptomics. Results Preliminary adoptive transfer experiments showed that, when assessed in bulk, the ratio of CXCR6-deficient to wild-type P14 CD8+ T cells was lower among siIELs at day 7 after acute infection. Notably, within this population at the same time point, CXCR6 deficiency led to reduced CD69 expression and a reciprocal increase in CD103. Conclusion Together, these findings suggest that CXCR6 plays a role in maintaining immune homeostasis and supporting the adaptive immune response in the gut during the early stages of acute infection. papers.title: Use of Geospatial Big Data Intelligence Software for Epidemic Forecasting and Public Health Decision-Making:
papers.abstract: Background Surveillance of infectious diseases remains a persistent challenge in many countries across the world. Most of these countries have slow reporting systems, poor infrastructure of data, and a limited capability of predictive analytics. Conventional surveillance methods are reactive, which leads to delayed outbreak containment. The development and assessment of a machine learning-driven early warning system for infectious disease prediction using geospatial big data from South-Western Nigeria, at the level of Local Government Area. Methods A longitudinal dataset comprising 152,438 observations (2020-2024) across 30 LGAs in six states was analyzed. The confirmed figures of COVID-19, Cholera, Lassa Fever, Malaria and Ebola, mobility index, temperature, rainfall, population density and location data. The study utilized Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and ARIMA. We evaluated the performance of our model based on Accuracy, Precision and Recall. A module for the detection of anomalies. Results According to the results, Random Forest had the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.94; F1-score = 0.91) followed by Gradient Boosting (AUC = 0.92; F1-score = 0.89). Moderate performance (AUC = 0.84) by Logistic Regression. ARIMA was able to capture trends over time but considerably underperformed at outbreak spikes (RMSE = 18.7). Mobility index and rainfall were necessary predictors (p < 0.05). Detection framework identified outbreak spikes with 93% sensitivity. Conclusion Machine learning early warning systems outperform conventional surveillance systems in developing countries. The fusion of environmental and mobility variables helps in prediction and containment at source. The framework provides a huge scalable and efficient resource model for digital disease surveillance in countries

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the persistent challenge of infectious disease surveillance in countries with slow reporting systems and limited predictive analytics capabilities. It evaluated a machine learning-driven early warning system using geospatial big data from South-Western Nigeria, analyzing a longitudinal dataset of 152,438 observations across 30 LGAs from 2020 to 2024. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景 监测 传染病仍然是世界许多国家面临的持续挑战。该研究旨在解决传统 监测 方法的局限性,这些方法是反应性的并导致 暴发 遏制延迟。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在尼日利亚西南部进行,分析了一个纵向数据集,该数据集包含 2020 年至 2024 年期间六个州 30 个地方政府区域 (LGA) 的 152,438 个观测数据。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究利用逻辑回归 (LR)、随机森林 (RF)、梯度提升机 (GBM) 和 ARIMA 来开发和评估机器学习驱动的早期预警系统,用于使用地理空间大数据进行传染病预测。该框架纳入了环境和流动性变量作为预测因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 随机森林表现出最高的预测性能,AUC 为 0.94,F1 得分为 0.91,其次是梯度提升,AUC 为 0.92,F1 得分为 0.89。Logistic 回归显示出中等性能 (AUC = 0.84),而 ARIMA 捕捉了随时间变化的趋势,但在 暴发 峰值时表现不佳 (RMSE = 18.7)。检测框架以 93% 的灵敏度识别出 暴发 尖峰。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在发展中国家,机器学习预警系统的性能优于传统的 监测 系统。环境和流动变量的融合有助于从源头进行预测和遏制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,将地理空间大数据与机器学习相结合可以改善传染病的预测和遏制,为基础设施有限的国家的数字疾病 监测 提供可扩展且高效的资源模型。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其重点关注尼日利亚西南部而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。由于使用单一数据集且缺乏外部验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Optimized arenavirus vectors with tumor-tropic mutations as new class of amplificators of anti-tumoral T cell responses 2259607
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Recent understandings of anti-tumoral immune mechanisms reveal a critical role for strong and sustainable activation of CD8+ T cells for successful immunotherapy. Recently, we showed that the non-cytopathic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) induces strong anti-tumor responses without directly killing tumor cells but by activation of CD8+ T cells. Here, we aim to generate an optimized arenavirus based on LCMV for application in cancer patients and its potential benefit with combination therapies. Methods We performed multiple passaging of the wild-type strain LCMV-WE in several murine and human cancer cells. The occurring mutations were identified and their role tested in vitro and in vivo in attenuated reassortant LCMV. Results We identified several mutations, which showed accelerated propagation in cancer cells leading to an attenuated reassortant arenavirus strain with accelerated entry in a broad spectrum of human cancer cells. This strain exhibited strong anti-tumoral efficacy in a variety of tumor models with minimal replication in healthy tissues and no severe disease symptoms in immune compromised murine model systems. Dissecting the anti-tumoral mechanism revealed that tumor-specific T cells were expanded, recruited to tumors and differentiated into potent effector cells. Furthermore, this virus strain amplified the anti-tumoral activity of a BiTE (Trp1/CD3) and combination with CAR- T cells to increase anti-tumor efficacy. In non-human primates, treatment with this strain led to increase in virus-mediated cytokine levels as well as T cells in the blood by maintaining a safe application. Conclusion In conclusion, by using the biological principle of mutation and selection, we developed an arenavirus-based immune therapy safely applied in preclinical model systems and GLP studies as well as harboring a unique mode of action and anti-tumoral efficacy. Combination with T cell-directed therapies including BITEs and CAR-T cells resulted in strong synergistic anti-tumoral responses. Funding Source Abalos Therapeutics; BMBF KMUi Topic Categories Translational and Interventional Immunology (TI)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Recent understandings of anti-tumoral immune mechanisms reveal a critical role for strong and sustainable activation of CD8+ T cells for successful immunotherapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved multiple passaging of the wild-type strain LCMV-WE in several murine and human cancer cells to generate an optimized arenavirus for cancer therapy.
analysis.methods: We performed multiple passaging of the wild-type strain LCMV-WE in several murine and human cancer cells, identified mutations, and tested their role in vitro and in vivo in attenuated reassortant LCMV.
analysis.main_results: We identified several mutations that showed accelerated propagation in cancer cells, leading to an attenuated reassortant arenavirus strain with accelerated entry in a broad spectrum of human cancer cells, which exhibited strong anti-tumoral efficacy in various tumor models with minimal replication in healthy tissues.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the optimized arenavirus strain safely amplifies anti-tumoral T cell responses and synergizes with T cell-directed therapies, representing a unique mode of action in cancer immunotherapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of arenavirus-based immune therapies for cancer patients, particularly in combination with existing T cell-directed therapies like BiTEs and CAR-T cells, to enhance anti-tumor efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted in preclinical model systems and GLP studies, with limited data on human applications and long-term safety.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed an optimized arenavirus vector based on lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) for cancer immunotherapy. By passaging LCMV-WE in cancer cells, researchers identified mutations that accelerated viral entry and replication in tumor cells while minimizing replication in healthy tissues. The resulting strain demonstrated strong anti-tumoral efficacy by expanding and activating tumor-specific T cells, with synergistic effects when combined with BiTE and CAR-T cell therapies. Preclinical studies in murine and non-human primate models confirmed safety and efficacy, supporting its potential as a novel cancer immunotherapy.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 最近对抗肿瘤免疫机制的理解揭示了 CD8+ T 细胞的强力和可持续激活对于成功的免疫治疗至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及野生型菌株 LCMV-WE 在几种小鼠和人类癌细胞中的多次传代,以生成用于癌症治疗的优化 沙粒病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 我们在几种鼠和人癌细胞中对野生型菌株 LCMV-WE 进行了多次传代,鉴定了 突变,并在体外和体内测试了它们在减毒重配 LCMV 中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们鉴定了几种在癌细胞中表现出加速增殖的 突变,从而产生了减毒重​​配 沙粒病毒 菌株,可加速进入广谱人类癌细胞,其在各种肿瘤模型中表现出强大的抗肿瘤功效,而在健康组织中的复制极少。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,优化的 沙粒病毒 菌株可以安全地放大抗肿瘤 T 细胞反应,并与 T 细胞定向疗法产生协同作用,代表了癌症免疫治疗中独特的作用模式。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为癌症患者开发基于 沙粒病毒 的免疫疗法提供了信息,特别是与现有的 T 细胞导向疗法(如 BiTE 和 CAR-T 细胞)相结合,以增强抗肿瘤功效。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在临床前模型系统和 GLP 研究中进行的,关于人体应用和长期安全性的数据有限。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 最近对抗肿瘤免疫机制的理解揭示了 CD8+ T 细胞的强力和可持续激活对于成功的免疫治疗至关重要。最近,我们发现非细胞病变的 淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 不直接杀死肿瘤细胞,而是通过激活 CD8+ T 细胞来诱导强烈的抗肿瘤反应。在这里,我们的目标是基于 LCMV 生成优化的 沙粒病毒,用于癌症患者及其联合疗法的潜在益处。方法 我们在几种小鼠和人类癌细胞中对野生型 LCMV-WE 株进行了多次传代。鉴定了出现的 突变 并在体外和体内测试了它们在减毒重配 LCMV 中的作用。结果我们鉴定了几种 突变,它们显示出在癌细胞中加速增殖,导致减毒重配 沙粒病毒 菌株加速进入广谱人类癌细胞。该菌株在多种肿瘤模型中表现出强大的抗肿瘤功效,在健康组织中复制极少,并且在免疫受损的小鼠模型系统中没有严重的疾病症状。剖析抗肿瘤机制表明,肿瘤特异性 T 细胞被扩增、招募到肿瘤并分化为有效的效应细胞。此外,该病毒株还增强了BiTE(Trp1/CD3)的抗肿瘤活性,并与CAR-T细胞结合以提高抗肿瘤功效。在非人类灵长类动物中,通过保持安全应用,使用该菌株的 治疗 导致病毒介导的细胞因子水平以及血液中 T 细胞的水平增加。结论 总之,我们利用突变的生物学原理和选择,开发了一种基于沙粒病毒的免疫疗法,可安全地应用于临床前模型系统和GLP研究,并具有独特的作用模式和抗肿瘤功效。与 BITE 和 CAR-T 细胞等 T 细胞定向疗法相结合,产生了强大的协同抗肿瘤反应。资金来源 Abalos Therapeutics;BMBF KMUi 主题类别 转化和介入免疫学 (TI)

papers.title: IRF2 deletion in regulatory T cells enhances anti-viral and anti-tumor immune responses 2257347
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction T regulatory cells (Tregs) are vital to limit immunopathology, yet they can also be an immune deterrent during chronic infections and cancer. Interferon Regulatory Factor 2 (IRF2) is a transcription factor that negatively regulates type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling. In response to viral infections, Tregs integrate IFN-I signals to limit their activity and enable antiviral immunity. Methods To understand how IRF2 alters Treg activity during chronic infections, we generated mice with Treg-specific conditional knockout (cKO) of IRF2 and infected them with chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV). Mouse melanoma models were used to study role in cancer. Results After infection, Treg numbers were almost entirely abolished in cKO mice, and the few remaining Tregs exhibited high IFN-I signaling and an activated phenotype. Lack of IRF2 expression by Tregs reduced CD8 T precursor exhausted (Tpex) cells and increased the amount and functional activity of effector virus-specific CD8 T cells. cKO mice also had more functional virus-specific CD4 T cells with a skew toward Th1 differentiation during chronic infection. Consistent with the diminished CD8 T cell exhaustion programming in chronic LCMV infection, ∼50% of cKO mice died within the first 2 weeks of infection, while the surviving mice exhibited decreased virus titers and accelerated control of the chronic infection. In response to melanoma, IRF2-deficiency in Tregs enabled better tumor control and substantially extended overall survival. Conclusion Thus, IRF2-serves as a key checkpoint in Tregs to balance IFN-I signaling, with important implications toward immune mediated control of chronic infections and cancer. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Tumor Immunology: Cellular Responses and Tumor Microevironment (TIME)
